spec_evidence: Annex F.6.10.2, UID asam.net:xodr:1.4.0:road.elevation.elev_along_ref_line: "Roads shall be elevated along their road reference line." XSD t_road_elevationProfile_elevation (OpenDRIVE_Road.xsd, complexType definition): <elevation> is defined solely by @s (s-coordinate on the road reference line, t_grEqZero) plus poly3 coefficients @a/@b/@c/@d (xs:double) -- no alternate elevation representation (no x/y/z override, no other coordinate frame) exists anywhere in the schema.
ambiguity_source: No XSD-valid OpenDRIVE document can violate this sentence: <elevation> can ONLY be authored as a poly3(s) height profile keyed to the road-reference-line s-coordinate -- there is no other attribute, element, or coordinate system through which an author could define elevation 'not along the reference line.' This is logical unfalsifiability by construction (every legal instance is tautologically compliant), not an interpretive judgment call the spec merely leaves open.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.12.24, UID asam.net:xodr:1.9.0:road.lane.road_mark.only_outer: "<roadMark> elements shall only be used to describe the outer lane marking." Chapter 11.9 Lane road markings: "<roadMark> ... Defines the style of the line at the outer border of a lane" and "The road marking information defines the style of the line at the lane's outer border. For left lanes, this is the left border, for right lanes the right one." Table 48 attribute list of <roadMark> (color/height/laneChange/material/sOffset/type/weight/width) has no inner/outer selector.
ambiguity_source: <roadMark> has no attribute distinguishing 'inner' vs 'outer' intent -- by the element's own normative definition, every <roadMark> child of a <lane> unconditionally describes that lane's outer border. No XSD-legal document can represent a 'non-outer' roadMark, so there is no violation state to detect structurally. Same unfalsifiable-by-construction shape as elev_along_ref_line.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.16.6, UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.object.bridges.define_type: "Bridges may be restricted to certain lanes, using the <laneValidity> element." Chapter 13.12 Bridges: "Bridges are valid for a road's complete cross section unless a lane validity record with further restrictions is provided as child element." -- permissive 'may', matched by the actual optional (0..*) <validity> child element in the schema.
ambiguity_source: Purely informative/permissive sentence documenting an available modeling option (attach a <validity> element under <bridge> to restrict lane applicability); it forbids nothing and there is no alternate mechanism to restrict a bridge to lanes that this text is guarding against, so no XML state constitutes a violation.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.16.8, UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.object.material.materials_may_differ: "The material of objects may differ from the surrounding road." Chapter 13.5 Object material, Table 96: <material> attributes (friction, roadMarkColor, roughness, surface) are all optional and application-defined ("The values depend on the application and are not defined in ASAM OpenDRIVE").
ambiguity_source: Permissive 'may differ' grant with no counterpart 'surrounding road material' value even present in a schema-comparable form (surface/friction/roughness are opaque app-defined strings/numbers with no cross-reference to a road-level material record) -- no violation condition exists to encode.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.16.13, UID asam.net:xodr:1.8.0:road.object.skeleton.vertex_local.linear_interpolation: "Values of @radius or @width and @length attributes will be interpolated linearly between two <vertexLocal> points." XSD t_road_objects_object_skeleton_polyline_vertexLocal (OpenDRIVE_Object.xsd): attributes are radius/intersectionPoint/id/u/v/z only -- no interpolation-mode or shape attribute exists.
ambiguity_source: Descriptive statement of consumer/renderer-side processing behavior (how a reader interpolates between two authored vertex points), not an author-facing prohibition -- there is no attribute through which an author could specify a non-linear interpolation, so no XML state can violate it; matches use_radius_or_width_length's coverage but adds nothing independently checkable.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.16.13, UID asam.net:xodr:1.9.0:road.object.skeleton.vertex_road.linear_interpolation: "Values of @radius or @width and @length attributes shall be interpolated linearly between two <vertexRoad> points." XSD t_road_objects_object_skeleton_polyline_vertexRoad (OpenDRIVE_Object.xsd): attributes dz/radius/intersectionPoint/id/s/t only -- again no interpolation-mode attribute.
ambiguity_source: Same consumer-side rendering semantics as the vertexLocal counterpart. The wording upgrades 'will' (1.8, vertexLocal) to 'shall' (1.9, vertexRoad) but the content is identical processing guidance -- verified directly against both XSD attribute sets, neither exposes any way for an author to select an alternative to linear interpolation, so no violation is representable in either case.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.17.2, UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.railroad.rail_lane_width_validity: "The width of the lane shall be at least the width rail-bound vehicles." (verbatim, grammatically missing 'of'; no numeric value for rail-bound-vehicle width is given anywhere in the OpenDRIVE 1.9 spec). Lane @type enum (OpenDRIVE_Lane.xsd, e_laneType) includes 'tram' and 'rail'. <width> is t_road_lanes_laneSection_lr_lane_width with @a/@b/@c/@d as unconstrained xs:double (OpenDRIVE_Lane.xsd) -- the schema itself does not forbid a<=0; the separate, distinct sibling checker rule road.lane.width.lane_width_validity (F.6.12) only requires width(ds)>=0 for ALL lanes generically, i.e. it permits exactly 0.
check_logic: For every <lane> with @type in {"rail","tram"} inside every road/lanes/laneSection/{left,center,right} group, for each of its <width> child elements read @a (the width value at that segment's local ds=0). Flag a violation if float(@a) <= 0 for any such width segment belonging to a rail/tram lane. Rationale: a real rail-bound vehicle necessarily has strictly positive width, so a rail/tram lane whose authored width touches zero or goes negative at a segment start can never satisfy 'at least the width of rail-bound vehicles,' regardless of what the (spec-unspecified) vehicle-width constant actually equals -- this is provable without needing that missing numeric threshold. (A stricter variant would also sample a+b*ds+c*ds^2+d*ds^3 across each segment's [0, next-sOffset) span to catch a mid-segment dip below zero, but the ds=0 check alone already recovers the clear-cut degenerate case using pure attribute reads, no geometry/network context needed.) Grounded against GT_esmini/test/odr_fixtures/official/examples/Ex_Railway-Station/Ex_Railway-Station.xodr: both tram lanes have @a=2.5, correctly non-violating.
ambiguity_source: The actual normative threshold -- 'the width of rail-bound vehicles' -- is never given a numeric value anywhere in the OpenDRIVE 1.9 spec (no reference vehicle width, no cited standard), and real rail/tram vehicle widths vary substantially (fixture evidence: Ex_Railway-Station.xodr uses a=2.5 for tram; prior investigation independently found ~2.5m tram vs ~3.5m heavy-rail in the corpus). Above the provable 'non-positive is definitely too narrow' floor, choosing any specific positive cutoff is an unresolvable external-knowledge/judgment call the spec does not make -- including the disputing auditor's own suggested '~1.435m standard gauge' proxy, which additionally conflates rail *gauge* (the distance between the two rails) with vehicle *width* (a different physical quantity entirely), so it should not be adopted even as a heuristic.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.21.1, UID asam.net:xodr:1.4.0:road.type.create_new_type_in_parent: "When the type of road changes, a new <type> element shall be created within the parent <road> element." Chapter 10.4 Road type: "The road type is valid for the entire road cross section ... One road type remains valid until another road type is defined." <type> (t_road_type, multiplicity 0..*) is the sole element representing road type at any s.
ambiguity_source: Because <type> is the ONLY mechanism through which a road's type value is expressed, a 'change' in road type is, by definition, always and exclusively representable by authoring a new <type> element -- there is no alternate way to change the effective type without adding the element, so no XSD-legal document can violate this sentence (unfalsifiable by construction, same shape as elev_along_ref_line). Separately, the auditor-suggested proxy ('flag identical consecutive <type>+<speed> as redundant') tests a different, unstated rule (no superfluous duplicate elements) rather than this rule's actual forward-direction obligation, and was independently shown to false-positive on 9/10 real occurrences in the official ASAM corpus -- further evidence no sound structural signature exists for the rule as written.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.21.3, UID asam.net:xodr:1.4.0:road.type.lane_type_may_differ_from_parent: "Single lanes may have another type than the road they belong to. Road type and lane type represent different properties and are both valid if specified."
ambiguity_source: Purely permissive design-freedom statement that explicitly declares any lane-type/road-type combination valid ('both valid if specified') -- there is no forbidden state described, so no violation condition exists to encode.

spec_evidence: map_rules.html F.6.19.1, UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.signal.priority: "If present, signals shall be used in priority to other traffic rules." Restated verbatim in 14_01_introduction.html §14.1 general 'Rules' list for <signals> (not tied to any specific element/attribute in that list; it sits beside road.signal.signal_type and road.signal.use_country_code as a generic prose rule for the whole <signal> concept).
ambiguity_source: The text prescribes runtime/consumer behavior -- a driving simulator or traffic-rule engine must give a physically-present <signal>'s regulation precedence over an inferred default traffic rule (e.g. default right-of-way) when both would otherwise apply at the same location. Nothing in the OpenDRIVE schema encodes 'priority relative to other traffic rules': there is no attribute, enumeration, or structural relationship on <signal> (checked t_road_signals_signal in OpenDRIVE_Signal.xsd -- id/type/subtype/value/orientation/country/etc., none express precedence-over-implicit-rules) that this statement could be validated against. Any two structurally valid OpenDRIVE files are indistinguishable with respect to this rule -- it is a behavioral directive to the consuming application, not a constraint on file structure. No XML-only pass/fail is constructible.

spec_evidence: map_rules.html F.6.19.6, UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.signal.dependency.multiple_dependency: "A signal may have multiple dependencies." Elaborated in 14_03_signal_dependency.html §14.3: "<dependency> ... Multiplicity: 0..*" / "One signal may have multiple dependencies." XSD: OpenDRIVE_Signal.xsd declares <xs:element name="dependency" type="t_road_signals_signal_dependency" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded"/> in BOTH t_road_signals_signal (line 360, the <signal> element itself) and t_road_signals_board (line 289, the <staticBoard>/<vmsBoard> sub-elements) -- i.e. every place a <dependency> can appear already permits 0..N unconditionally, with no other schema constraint (no xs:unique/xs:key capping count) anywhere that could restrict it.
check_logic: This is a permissive cardinality statement that is already fully and unconditionally granted by the XSD, not a prohibition. Algorithm: for every <signal> element (and, for completeness, every <staticBoard>/<vmsBoard> board sub-element) in the document, count(./dependency) may be any value 0..N -- there is no condition on that count, or on any other structural feature, that the rule text forbids. Consequently the deterministic checker is: iterate all <signal>/<staticBoard>/<vmsBoard> nodes, and PASS unconditionally regardless of dependency count -- no XML instance that is otherwise schema-valid can violate this specific rule (a violation would require the schema itself to cap count(./dependency) at 1, which it does not; maxOccurs='unbounded' at both occurrence sites confirms this). Note for the ledger: because no failing input is constructible, this rule has zero discriminating power as a lint check and should likely be marked 'not independently actionable / subsumed by XSD' rather than implemented as a real checker function, but the verdict per the requested taxonomy is DETERMINISTIC because the pass/fail algorithm (trivial as it is) is complete and fully derived from XML structure alone, confirming the prior pass's own reasoning was correct on the facts even though it filed this under 'gap_ambiguous'.

spec_evidence: map_rules.html F.6.19.7, UID asam.net:xodr:1.9.0:road.signal.gantry.all_variable_boards_same_gantry: "All variable message boards within a <vmsGroup> element shall belong to the same gantry." 14_07_signal_boards.html §14.7.4 Gantry: <vmsGroup> (t_signalGroup_vmsGroup, introduced 1.8.0) contains 1..* <vmsBoardReference> (t_signalGroup_vmsBoardReference: @signalId 'Id of the signal that has a <vmsBoard> assigned', @vmsIndex, @groupIndex). XSD: <vmsGroup> is declared as a TOP-LEVEL child of <OpenDRIVE> itself (OpenDRIVE_Core.xsd line 35: maxOccurs='unbounded' minOccurs='0'), not nested inside any <road> or <object type="gantry">, and carries no roadId/gantryId attribute of its own (only @id, its own identity). <object type="gantry"> is a plain roadside <object> (13_14_object_examples.html §13.14.4) with no attribute referencing signals or vmsGroups. <signal> (t_road_signals_signal, OpenDRIVE_Signal.xsd line 352+) has an optional 0..* <reference elementType="object"|"signal" elementId="..."/> child (14_04_signal_reference.html §14.4: "Signal references link a signal to another signal or object... The type of reference is not specifically defined in ASAM OpenDRIVE and may be set in the application... Rules regarding the type of reference are defined in the application and are not stored in ASAM OpenDRIVE.") -- generic and not gantry-specific; the spec's own worked example uses it for a stop-line, not a gantry. Empirically, this repo's own 1.9 fixture GT_esmini/test/odr_fixtures/handauthored/21_boards_vmsgroup_19.xodr groups two vmsBoard-bearing <signal>s (id=1,2) into one <vmsGroup> with NO <object type="gantry"> element anywhere in the file and NO <reference> child on either signal -- gantry membership is expressed only by informal co-location (same road id=1, same s=120.0, different t).
ambiguity_source: The auditor's disputed suggestion had two parts; only the first is a genuine structural check. Part (b) -- 'referenced signals ... share the same (road id, s) within a small tolerance (a gantry = one road cross-section)' -- requires inventing a numeric proximity tolerance the spec never states, and treating 'same road + nearby s' as the definition of 'same gantry', which is an authoring convention, not a normative XSD/prose rule; a physically real gantry could legitimately have boards mounted with different s if the gantry structure spans a curve, and the 1.1 <reference elementType="object"> mechanism that COULD make the gantry link ID-exact is optional, free-text-typed, and absent from this repo's own reference fixture, so its presence cannot be assumed. Determining true gantry membership therefore requires either (i) geometric/tolerance judgment on s/t co-location that the spec leaves entirely open, or (ii) trusting an optional, semantically-unconstrained <reference> link whose use for this exact purpose is never mandated -- both are interpretive calls beyond pure XML structure.
check_logic: Checkable sub-case (structural precondition for the rule to even be evaluable, matching auditor suggestion part (a)): (1) Build a dict of signal_id -> <signal> element by collecting every <signal id="..."> under every <road>/<signals> in the document (xpath .//road/signals/signal). (2) Build a set has_vmsboard = {id for id,elem in dict if elem.find('vmsBoard') is not None}. (3) For every top-level <vmsGroup> child of <OpenDRIVE>, for every child <vmsBoardReference signalId="X">: flag a VIOLATION if X not in dict (dangling/unresolved signalId -- the referenced 'variable message board' does not exist) OR X in dict but X not in has_vmsboard (the referenced signal exists but has no <vmsBoard> child, i.e. it is not actually a variable message board and so cannot meaningfully 'belong to the same gantry' as a VMS group member). This is fully decidable from XML structure alone (element/attribute lookups only) and catches a real, common authoring defect (typo'd or stale signalId, or referencing a static-only signal), but it validates reference integrity and VMS-board-ness, not 'same gantry' itself -- see ambiguity_source for the uncovered part.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.12.22 UID asam.net:xodr:1.4.0:road.lane.link.no_link: "The <link> element shall be omitted if the lane starts or ends in a junction or has no link." Chapter 11.6 'Lane linkage' (11_lanes/11_06_lane_link.html) restates it as a positive permission: "This element may only be omitted, if lanes end at a junction or have no physical link." Both of the two natural XML-structural readings are falsified by official ASAM reference content: (1) reading 'omitted' literally as tag-absence is falsified because essentially every lane in the corpus (incl. ASAM's own official examples, e.g. every lane in GT_esmini/test/odr_fixtures/official/examples/Ex_Slip_Lane/Ex_Slip_Lane.xodr) uses an empty placeholder <link>\n</link> rather than true omission -- confirmed directly by inspection, matching the prior pass's reported 907 false positives; (2) reading 'starts/ends in a junction' as 'the road's own <link><predecessor|successor elementType="junction"> at that end' is falsified by the very same file: road id="77" has <link><predecessor elementType="junction" elementId="2"/><successor elementType="junction" elementId="3"/></link> (both ends terminate in junctions per road-level linkage) yet its driving lane id="-1" carries a populated, legitimate <link><predecessor id="-4"/><successor id="-4"/></link> -- a real, sanctioned direct lane link at a junction-adjacent road, independently reproducing the prior investigation's Ex_Slip_Lane counter-example.
ambiguity_source: Distinguishing 'physically-connected, unambiguous lane linkage legitimately expressed at lane level despite the road formally touching a junction' (the slip-lane connector road 77 pattern, sanctioned by ASAM's own official example) from 'a lane link that should have been omitted and resolved purely via the junction's <connection>/<laneLink> graph' requires reconstructing and judging the junction's full connectivity topology plus real-world physical continuity -- no XML attribute encodes this distinction. Separately, whether the spec's 'omitted' means true tag-absence or permits an empty placeholder <link/> is itself left undefined and both readings are contradicted by trusted corpus content, so even the weaker literal-omission reading is not enforceable.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.12.22 UID asam.net:xodr:1.4.0:road.lane.link.use_junctions: "Two lanes shall only be linked if their linkage is clear. If the relationship to a predecessor or successor is ambiguous, junctions shall be used." Listed verbatim under 'Rules' in Chapter 11.6 (11_lanes/11_06_lane_link.html) with no further operational definition of 'clear' vs 'ambiguous' anywhere in Ch.11 or Ch.12. The road-level sibling rule in 10_roads/10_03_road_linkage.html, asam.net:xodr:1.4.0:road.linkage.is_junction_needed ("Two roads shall only be linked directly if the linkage is clear. If the relationship to successor or predecessor is ambiguous, junctions shall be used."), is the identical judgment pattern one level up, confirming the spec never attaches a checkable predicate to 'ambiguous' at either granularity. The same Ex_Slip_Lane road id=77 (direct, non-junction-mediated lane link -predecessor/successor id=-4- at a road whose own road-level linkage terminates at junctions on both ends) is official, sanctioned proof that a direct lane link adjacent to a junction is commonly legitimate, so any naive 'junction-adjacent direct link = ambiguous' structural proxy would misfire on trusted reference data, mirroring the prior pass's corpus-scan finding.
ambiguity_source: 'Clear' vs 'ambiguous' relationship to a predecessor/successor is a real-world-topology/authorial-intent judgment (would a driver's or router's continuation onto that specific lane be unambiguous) with no corresponding XML attribute. A structural proxy would require reconstructing the whole road-network graph (every road's <link> elements plus every junction's <connection>/<laneLink> topology) and then judging whether a structurally-plausible alternative constitutes genuine real-world ambiguity -- squarely a topology/geometry-dependent judgment call the spec text never reduces to an attribute-level test, and the Ex_Slip_Lane counter-example shows naive proxies over-fire on legitimate official content.

spec_evidence: Annex F.6.12.11 UID asam.net:xodr:1.4.0:road.lane.lane_reverse_left_right: "@direction=\"reverse\" shall not be used to change from right-hand traffic to left-hand traffic and vice versa." Chapter 11.3.1 'Driving direction' (11_lanes/11_03_lane_groups.html) gives the exact default-direction formulas that make this checkable: for @rule="RHT", <right> lanes (negative id) default forward and <left> lanes (positive id) default backward; for @rule="LHT" it is the reverse; "The @direction='reversed' attribute reverses the default driving direction" per lane. Road/@rule is optional with a documented default of RHT when absent (OpenDRIVE_Road.xsd: "When this attribute is missing, RHT is assumed."). e_lane_direction (OpenDRIVE_Lane.xsd) enumerates standard/reversed/both. t_road_lanes_laneSection (OpenDRIVE_Lane.xsd) makes <left> and <right> each minOccurs=0, with the doc note "at least one <right> or <left>" required -- single-sided laneSections are legal and expected. Algebraically substituting the RHT formula with every lane's direction flipped yields exactly the LHT formula (right=backward, left=forward) and vice versa -- i.e. marking every driving lane on BOTH <left> and <right> as reversed within one laneSection reproduces, bit-for-bit, the net driving-direction assignment of swapping @rule, which is precisely the prohibited action. Verified against the corpus: only 2 files repo-wide use direction="reversed" at all (GT_esmini/test/odr_fixtures/handauthored/09_lane_attributes_18.xodr and its build/ copy); that fixture has exactly 1 of 2 actual type="driving" lanes reversed (id=2 left driving reversed, id=-1 right driving standard) -- correctly NOT matching the both-sides-all-reversed signature, confirming no false positive on the one known real-world exemplar, consistent with the prior pass's own finding that this specific fixture is legitimate single-lane contraflow.
check_logic: For each <road>/<lanes>/<laneSection>: collect left_driving = <left>/<lane> elements with @type='driving' (empty list if no <left>), and right_driving = <right>/<lane> elements with @type='driving' (empty list if no <right>). Only evaluate laneSections where BOTH left_driving and right_driving are non-empty (a laneSection with driving lanes on only one side has no RHT/LHT counterpart to swap against and is out of scope). For such two-sided laneSections, flag a violation if EVERY lane in left_driving UNION right_driving has @direction == 'reversed' (attribute present and literally 'reversed'; absent or 'standard' or 'both' does not count). This is independent of the road's own @rule value -- the equivalence holds symmetrically in both directions per the 11.3.1 formulas. No geometry is needed; only <road>, <lanes>/<laneSection>/<left|right>/<lane>@type, and <lane>@direction are read.
ambiguity_source: The check only catches the airtight 100%-both-sides-reversed signature. Any partial or mixed reversal (some but not all driving lanes reversed, or reversal confined to one side only) is structurally indistinguishable between 'legitimate single/multi-lane contraflow' (the sanctioned use of @direction=reversed, per 11.3.1's own phrasing and the one real fixture found) and 'a sloppy/partial attempt to fake a hand-of-traffic change' -- the spec supplies no threshold or additional attribute to arbitrate that residual space, so it remains a genuine authorial-intent judgment call outside the deterministic sub-case.

spec_evidence: Annex F UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.signal.validity.right_hand_traffic_lane_ids (map_rules.html line ~4832): "For right-hand traffic, @orientation='+' implies that the <validity> element shall only span negative lane ids, while @orientation='-' implies that the <validity> element shall only span positive lane ids. If the given <validity> elements span both, positive and negative lane ids, @orientation='none' shall be used." Grounding attributes: road/@rule is e_trafficRule {RHT,LHT}, optional, XSD doc + 10_roads/10_01_introduction.html: "When this attribute is missing, RHT is assumed." signal/@orientation is e_orientation, REQUIRED (OpenDRIVE_Signal.xsd t_road_signals_signal, line 384: '+'=valid in positive s-direction, '-'=negative, 'none'=both). validity/@fromLane,@toLane are required xs:integer (OpenDRIVE_Lane.xsd t_road_objects_object_laneValidity). Sign convention: 11_lanes/11_03_lane_groups.html asam.net:xodr:1.4.0:road.lane.lanes_numbered_correctly: "Lanes with positive ID run on the left side of the center lane, while lanes with negative ID run on the right side", plus the RHT/LHT driving-direction paragraph: for RHT, +s-direction traffic runs on <right> (negative-id) lanes. 14_02_lane_validity_signals.html chains this rule directly under the umbrella asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.object.validty.check_parent_orientation ("range given by all <validity> elements shall be a subset of the parent's @orientation attribute") -- this LHT/RHT rule pair is literally the concrete definition of what that umbrella phrase means. Direct in-repo precedent: GT_esmini/docs/knowledge/opendrive_gap_checkers/check_road_object_core.py::run_checks already implements the textually-identical sibling rule for <object> (status=implemented_gt in opendrive_rule_ledger.yaml, lines ~1820-1827), using expect_neg=(orientation=='+') for RHT and firing on pos_present/neg_present computed exactly as here.
check_logic: For every <road> R (direct child of OpenDRIVE): road_rule = R.get('rule') or 'RHT'. This rule variant is active only when road_rule=='RHT'. For every <signal> S in R.find('signals').findall('signal'): orient = S.get('orientation'); skip if orient not in ('+','-'). Collect all <validity> children of S (S.findall('validity')); skip if none. For each validity v, parse fl=int(v.get('fromLane')), tl=int(v.get('toLane')) (skip malformed / fl>tl, that's a different rule's violation); lo,hi=min(fl,tl),max(fl,tl). Aggregate over ALL validity children of S: has_pos = True if any hi>=1 (a lane id >=1 -- 'positive/left' -- appears); has_neg = True if any lo<=-1 (a lane id <=-1 -- 'negative/right' -- appears). Lane id 0 (center lane) counts toward NEITHER has_pos nor has_neg (it is defined as neither positive nor negative by the lanes_numbered_correctly rule). expected = 'neg' if orient=='+' else 'pos' (RHT mapping). VIOLATION (flag road.signal.validity.right_hand_traffic_lane_ids) iff: (expected=='neg' and has_pos and not has_neg) or (expected=='pos' and has_neg and not has_pos) -- i.e. the signal's combined validity references real (non-zero) lane ids of ONLY the wrong sign, with no lane of the correct sign present anywhere among its own validity children. Do not flag when has_pos and has_neg are both True (validity genuinely spans real lanes on both sides) -- see ambiguity_source.
ambiguity_source: The rule's second sentence ("if the given <validity> elements span both, positive and negative lane ids, @orientation='none' shall be used") implies that ANY signal whose combined validity spans real lane ids on both sides while orientation != 'none' is ALSO a violation. I re-scanned the full official+handauthored+resources .xodr corpus (via a standalone xml.etree script) and found this exact 'spans-both' pattern recurring -- not as noise, but with clean, round, apparently-deliberate bounds -- in: UC_Simple-X-Junction-TrafficLights.xodr (6 signals, validity=(-3,3), sign type 306 'Vorfahrtstrasse'/priority-road and type 1000001 traffic-light-related, on ordinary bidirectional roads with real driving lanes on both sides); UC_2Lane-RoundAbout-3Arms.xodr (2 signals, validity=(-3,4), sign type 283 'Halteverbot nach'/no-stopping); GT's own resources/xodr/fabriksgatan_traffic_lights.xodr and its _ctrl variant (4 signals total, validity=(-1,1), a real traffic-light signal); and resources/xodr/straight_500m_signs.xodr (a signal split into a (-3,-1) validity child and a (1,3) validity child under the SAME <signal id=0>, i.e. spans-both via multiple <validity> elements rather than one wide range). Unlike the sibling <object> rule (already implemented_gt, 0 hits on the official corpus per its own status_reason), the <signal> variant's spans-both pattern is both more frequent and recurs for specific, plausible-looking sign SEMANTIC categories (road-status / no-stopping / traffic-light) whose real-world legal effect could legitimately apply to the whole road cross-section regardless of which lane the physical board faces. Annex F defines no attribute (nor references any sign-type catalog) that would let a checker distinguish 'this <validity> is a literal per-lane restriction' from 'this <validity> is a whole-cross-section span for a road-level-status sign' -- so whether to flag these per the rule's literal second sentence, or treat them as a legitimate authoring idiom the text simply doesn't anticipate, is an interpretive/policy judgment the spec leaves open, not resolvable from XML structure alone.

spec_evidence: Annex F UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.signal.validity.left_hand_traffic_lane_ids (map_rules.html line ~4817): "For left-hand-traffic, @orientation='-' implies that the <validity> element shall only span negative lane ids, while @orientation='+' implies that the <validity> element shall only span positive lane ids. If the given <validity> elements span both, positive and negative lane ids, @orientation='none' shall be used." Same grounding attributes/XSD as the right_hand mirror (road/@rule, signal/@orientation, validity/@fromLane,@toLane). Sign convention per 11_lanes/11_03_lane_groups.html: for LHT, +s-direction traffic runs on <left> (positive-id) lanes ('the default driving direction would be in positive direction of the road reference line for all <left> element lanes with positive @id attribute...for LHT'). In-repo precedent: check_road_object_core.py already implements road.object.validty.left_hand_traffic_lane_ids (status=implemented_gt) with expect_neg=(orientation=='-') for LHT, verified per its status_reason against a re-run synthetic self-test confirming both directions fire correctly (0 real LHT objects with validity exist in the corpus, so 0 findings there is expected, not a gap).
check_logic: Identical algorithm to road.signal.validity.right_hand_traffic_lane_ids, with two differences: (1) the rule variant is active only when road_rule == 'LHT' EXPLICITLY (road.get('rule')=='LHT'; the default when @rule is absent is RHT, so an unmarked road never triggers this variant); (2) the expected-sign mapping is flipped: expected = 'pos' if orient=='+' else 'neg' (LHT mapping -- '+' orientation implies positive/left lane ids only, '-' implies negative/right only). Same has_pos/has_neg aggregation over the signal's <validity> children, same lane-id-0-is-neutral treatment, same violation condition (wrong sign present, right sign absent), same 'spans-both' exclusion from this checkable sub-case.
ambiguity_source: Same residual as the right_hand mirror: the 'spans real lane ids on both sides while orientation != none' sub-case is left unresolved as a genuine interpretive judgment the spec text does not settle (see right_hand_traffic_lane_ids entry for the concrete official-corpus evidence of the whole-cross-section idiom). Confidence is 'med' rather than 'high' specifically because I could find ZERO real-world LHT road with any <signal><validity> content anywhere in the available corpus (the dedicated GT_esmini/test/odr_fixtures/lht/*.xodr fixtures, e.g. signals_orientation_lht_rht.xodr and 4way_priority_lht.xodr, use @orientation but carry no <validity> children at all) -- so while the mapping itself is directly spec-mandated and mirrors the already-shipped, synthetic-self-tested <object> LHT checker, I have no real corpus example (positive or negative) to empirically cross-check the LHT branch specifically, unlike the RHT branch which I traced down to concrete real violations and confirmed compliant cases.

spec_evidence: Annex F UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.signal.reference.right_hand_traffic_lane_ids (map_rules.html line ~4751), verbatim identical wording to the .validity variant but scoped to <signalReference> instead of <signal>. Structural placement: t_road_signals_signalReference (OpenDRIVE_Signal.xsd line ~642) is a direct sibling of <signal> under <road><signals> (t_road_signals, line 266: 'signal' and 'signalReference' are both direct children); it has its OWN required @orientation (e_orientation, same enum) and its own optional <validity> children (t_road_objects_object_laneValidity, same type as <signal>'s). 14_05_multiple_roads.html clarifies scope: 'The direction on the road for which the referenced signal is valid shall be specified for every <signalReference> element using the @orientation attribute' (asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.signal.reference.specify_direction) -- 'the road' = the road hosting this specific <signalReference> element, not necessarily the road hosting the original <signal> it points to via @id (the whole point of <signalReference> is cross-road reuse of one physical signal, per 14.5's introduction). check_parent_orientation is chained here too (map_rules.html / 14_05_multiple_roads.html line ~683), confirming the same 'validity subset of orientation' framework applies.
check_logic: For every <road> R: road_rule = R.get('rule') or 'RHT'; active only when road_rule=='RHT'. For every <signalReference> SR in R.find('signals').findall('signalReference') (note: R is the road PHYSICALLY CONTAINING this signalReference element, read via straightforward parent traversal -- NOT the road hosting the <signal> that SR/@id points to): orient = SR.get('orientation'); skip if not in ('+','-'). Aggregate has_pos/has_neg over SR.findall('validity') exactly as for <signal> (fromLane/toLane ints, lane id 0 neutral). expected = 'neg' if orient=='+' else 'pos'. VIOLATION iff (expected=='neg' and has_pos and not has_neg) or (expected=='pos' and has_neg and not has_pos). Same 'spans-both' exclusion as the .validity variant.
ambiguity_source: Same structural residual as the .validity variants (spans-both-signs sub-case is a spec-unresolved judgment call). Confidence 'med': across the entire searched corpus (official + handauthored + resources) I found exactly ONE real <signalReference> with any <validity> content at all -- GT_esmini/test/odr_fixtures/handauthored/19_signal_reference_18.xodr, road id=2 (rule absent -> RHT), signalReference id=1, orientation='+', validity=(-1,-1) -- which is fully compliant under this check_logic (negative-only, matches expected='neg'), so it corroborates the mapping but supplies no negative/violating example to stress-test against. The algorithm itself is not in doubt (it is structurally identical to the extensively-verified .validity case, just applied to a sibling element with the same attribute shapes), but the near-total absence of real signalReference/validity usage in any available fixture means the RHT branch here is less empirically exercised than road.signal.validity.right_hand_traffic_lane_ids.

spec_evidence: Annex F UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:road.signal.reference.left_hand_traffic_lane_ids (map_rules.html line ~4736), verbatim identical wording to the .validity LHT variant but scoped to <signalReference>. Same t_road_signals_signalReference XSD structure and 14_05_multiple_roads.html 'direction on the road ... using @orientation' scoping as the right_hand mirror above. Sign convention per 11_lanes/11_03_lane_groups.html LHT paragraph (same citation as road.signal.validity.left_hand_traffic_lane_ids).
check_logic: Identical algorithm to road.signal.reference.right_hand_traffic_lane_ids, with the same two LHT-specific differences as validity.left_hand vs validity.right_hand: (1) active only when road_rule=='LHT' explicitly (road hosting the <signalReference>, not the referenced <signal>'s road); (2) expected = 'pos' if orient=='+' else 'neg'. Same has_pos/has_neg aggregation, zero-neutral treatment, and 'wrong sign present, right sign absent' violation condition, same spans-both exclusion.
ambiguity_source: Same residual as the other three (spans-both-signs sub-case left as an interpretive judgment the spec does not resolve -- see road.signal.validity.right_hand_traffic_lane_ids for the concrete official-corpus evidence). Confidence 'med', for the same reason as reference.right_hand: the single real corpus example of a <signalReference> with <validity> content (handauthored/19_signal_reference_18.xodr) is RHT, not LHT, so this exact LHT branch has zero real-corpus grounding (positive or negative) beyond the spec text and structural symmetry with the already-shipped, synthetic-self-tested <object> LHT checker.

spec_evidence: Annex F.4.5.3 (map_rules.html, UID asam.net:xodr:1.9.0:junctions.common.not_only_two): "Junctions should not be used when only two roads meet." Same bullet repeated verbatim in 12_02_common_junctions.html's "Rules" list for common (type=default) junctions -- the rule is not repeated in 12_06_direct_junctions.html or 12_07_virtual_junctions.html, whose own Annex F sub-namespaces are junctions.direct.* / junctions.virtual.*. 12_13_junction_groups.html: "Junction groups indicate for routing that the grouped junctions belong to the same node and are commonly seen as one big junction, for example roundabouts or highway interchanges." 12_05_cross_paths.html / OpenDRIVE_Junction.xsd t_junction_crossPath: crossPath is only schema-legal as a child of <junction>. Empirically verified: a repo-wide scan of official+handauthored xodr fixtures found every <=2-road junction that is @type="direct" (Ex_Entry_Exit, Ex_Slip_Lane, UC_Motorway-Exit-Entry-DirectJunction) is out of this rule's scope, and the one @type="default" 2-road junction that IS grouped (handauthored/25_junction_group_15.xodr, junction id=100 referenced by <junctionGroup type="roundabout">) matches the junctionGroup exemption; handauthored/21_common_junction_crosspath_19.xodr shows a 2-road default junction whose only purpose is to host a <crossPath>.
check_logic: For every <junction> where @type is absent or @type="default": (1) roads = union of connection/@incomingRoad and connection/@connectingRoad across its <connection> children; (2) if len(roads) != 2, no finding; (3) if len(roads) == 2: exempt (no finding) if this junction's @id appears in any /OpenDRIVE/junctionGroup/junctionReference/@junction in the document, OR if the junction has >=1 <crossPath> child; otherwise flag as an advisory ("should"-level) finding: a common junction connecting exactly two roads with no documented structural justification. @type="direct" and @type="virtual" junctions are excluded from this rule entirely (separate Annex F sub-namespaces govern them, and 2-road direct junctions -- e.g. motorway on/off-ramps -- are their canonical, expected shape).
ambiguity_source: The exemption list (junctionGroup membership, crossPath-hosting) is not declared exhaustive by the spec text; other legitimate reasons for a 2-road common junction (e.g. hosting other junction-only features such as elevationGrid/boundary, or a deliberate lane-count/width transition needing laneLink flexibility a plain road link can't express) are conceivable and not enumerated, so a flag under this refined test is still only a candidate for human review, not a guaranteed violation.

spec_evidence: Annex F.4.5.5 (UID asam.net:xodr:1.4.0:junctions.common.when_to_use): "Junctions shall only be used when roads cannot be linked directly. They clarify ambiguities for the linking. Ambiguities are caused when a road has two or more possible predecessor or successor roads." Same text repeated in 12_02_common_junctions.html Rules list. Contrast with 12_05_cross_paths.html / F.4.8.6 junctions.cross_path.within_junction_area ("Cross paths shall be within the area of a common junction or a virtual junction") and the crossPath XSD parentage (only legal inside <junction>), which together demonstrate a junction can be legitimately required for reasons wholly unrelated to predecessor/successor routing ambiguity.
ambiguity_source: The operative test ("roads cannot be linked directly") is a whole-network counterfactual: it requires checking whether some other direct road-to-road <link><predecessor>/<successor> could have replaced the junction, i.e. reconstructing alternative routing candidates across the entire file's road graph and geometry, not just the roads declared inside this one junction. A locally-scoped proxy (does an @incomingRoad within this junction's own <connection> elements map to 2+ distinct @connectingRoad values) tests only the rule's second ("ambiguity") sentence and is largely redundant with the narrower, better-bounded not_only_two check; it cannot establish the first clause in general because junctions are independently and legitimately required for reasons the rule's own "ambiguity" framing does not cover (e.g. crossPath hosting, per the cross-reference above), so absence of internal branching does not prove a junction was unnecessary. No pure-XML test closes this gap without geometric/topological reconstruction of the whole network.

spec_evidence: Annex F.4.6.3 (UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:junctions.connection.lane_change_one_con_road): "By one connecting road with multiple <laneLink> elements for the connections between the lanes." Full context in 12_04_connecting_roads.html: "An incoming road with multiple lanes may be connected to the lanes of the road leading out off the junction in different ways:" followed by this bullet and its sibling (no_lane_change_for_mult_con_roads) as two enumerated alternatives -- no shall/shall-not language anywhere in the bullet or its introducing sentence.
ambiguity_source: This is a non-imperative descriptive enumeration of one of two valid, non-exclusive junction-modeling patterns (a file may use this pattern, the sibling pattern, or a mix across different lane groups within the same incoming/outgoing pair). There is no prescriptive condition to violate -- nothing in the XML structure can be flagged as non-compliant, because the sentence does not forbid or require anything.

spec_evidence: Annex F.4.6.5 (UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:junctions.connection.no_lane_change_for_mult_con_roads): "By multiple connecting roads, each with one <laneLink> element for the connection between two specific lanes. Lane changes within this junction are not possible." Same context as lane_change_one_con_road (12_04_connecting_roads.html): introduced by "...may be connected...in different ways:" as the companion enumerated bullet, again with no shall/shall-not language.
ambiguity_source: Same reasoning as the sibling rule: this is a descriptive statement of a consequence of a modeling pattern (multiple single-laneLink connecting roads inherently preclude in-junction lane changes -- a logical/mathematical fact about that pattern, not an authoring constraint), not a testable prescriptive rule. No violation predicate can be constructed from XML structure.

spec_evidence: Annex F.4.8.2 (UID asam.net:xodr:1.8.0:junctions.cross_path.disregard_cross_road_evelation): "The elevations of the crossing road defined by the @crossingRoad attribute of the <crossPath> element are disregarded." Same text in 12_05_cross_paths.html's Rules list, positioned among rules about how a <crossPath>'s geometry/consumption is computed (alongside within_junction_area, lane_linkage, start_end_contained) rather than about what an author may or must write.
ambiguity_source: This sentence describes consumer/processing semantics -- how a simulation engine or geometry-computation tool should treat the crossing road's elevation profile when rendering/consuming a <crossPath> (i.e., disregard it, presumably deriving elevation from the linked lanes instead) -- not a constraint on what an author's XML file may contain. There is no authored XML pattern (presence, absence, or value of any element/attribute) whose violation this sentence describes; it is guidance to the reader of the format, not the writer.

spec_evidence: Annex F.4.12.2 (UID asam.net:xodr:1.7.0:junctions.priority.no_signals): "<priority> elements should only be used if there are no signals defined." Context, 12_04_connecting_roads.html Sec 12.4.1: "The junction priority record provides information about the priority of one road over another road that are part of this junction. It is only required if priorities cannot be derived from signs or signals in a junction or on tracks leading to a junction." OpenDRIVE_Signal.xsd t_road_signals_signal, @dynamic attribute (required, t_yesNo): "Indicates whether the signal is dynamic or static. Example: traffic light is dynamic." Empirically: resources/scenario_authoring/road_catalog/generated/4way_priority__main_ns.xodr pairs 5 <priority> elements with 4 static signs (@dynamic="no", @type="205"/"306" -- DE yield/priority-road codes), i.e. no @dynamic="yes" signal present, so this trusted file does not contradict a dynamic-only reading. Also relevant/in tension: 14_01_introduction.html defines "Signals are traffic signs, traffic lights, and specific road marking..." (broad umbrella term including static signs) and Annex F road.signal.priority states "If present, signals shall be used in priority to other traffic rules," which textually supports a broader reading than dynamic-only.
check_logic: For every junction (type="default" or "virtual", both schema-legal parents of <priority> per OpenDRIVE_Junction.xsd) with >=1 <priority> child: (1) collect participating road IDs from connection/@incomingRoad, connection/@connectingRoad (and, for virtual junctions, @mainRoad); (2) for each such road id, look up <road id="..."> and inspect its <signals>/<signal> children; (3) if any such <signal> has @dynamic="yes", flag the junction -- a fixed/static <priority> ordering co-existing with a dynamically time-varying right-of-way device (e.g. a traffic light) is a direct logical-consistency conflict with the rationale given in 12.4.1, and this narrow condition is uncontested by any known corpus counter-example.
ambiguity_source: Whether the rule's unqualified "signals" also covers static signs (the textually broader reading, supported by 14.1's definition and the related road.signal.priority rule) is not resolved by the checker-rule prose itself. Applying that broad reading as a hard structural test directly contradicts established, trusted GT authoring practice (static priority/yield signs routinely paired with an explicit <priority> element, since the sign's type code alone doesn't give a simulation engine machine-readable road-vs-road ordering). Resolving which scope was intended is a genuine interpretive judgment the spec leaves open; only the @dynamic="yes" sub-case is safely checkable.

spec_evidence: Annex F.4.13.4 (UID asam.net:xodr:1.9.0:junctions.virtual.main_road_only): "Virtual junctions shall be used for branches off the main road only. The main road has priority if not specified otherwise." 12_07_virtual_junctions.html Table 69: @mainRoad "The main road from which the connecting roads of the virtual junction branch off. This attribute is mandatory for virtual junctions..." Same section's Rules list also states "Virtual junctions shall not replace common junctions and crossings that connect multiple roads." Spec's own worked example (12_07, mainRoad="1"): connectingRoad "2"'s <link><predecessor elementType="road" elementId="1" elementS="50"/> and connectingRoads "4"/"5" each have a <successor elementType="road" elementId="1" elementS="70"/> -- i.e. every connectingRoad directly references @mainRoad in its own road link. Verified against handauthored/23_virtual_junction_17.xodr: junction 888 mainRoad="1", connection id=0 incomingRoad="1"==mainRoad, and connectingRoad "2"'s own <link><predecessor elementId="1"> also references mainRoad directly.
check_logic: For every <junction @type="virtual">: (1) referential integrity -- @mainRoad must equal the @id of some <road> element in the document; flag if not found. (2) participation -- flag if NEITHER holds: (a) some <connection>/@incomingRoad == @mainRoad, or (b) some <connection>/@connectingRoad resolves to a <road id=connectingRoad> whose own <link><predecessor|successor elementType="road"> has @elementId == @mainRoad. Both checks are pure XML/attribute lookups requiring no coordinate geometry.
ambiguity_source: The rule's exclusivity clause -- that the junction is used for branches off the main road ONLY, i.e. that every other road drawn into the junction (such as an intermediate road like "99" in the spec's own parking-lot example, which is itself neither @mainRoad nor directly link-referencing it) is a legitimate branch/sub-branch of that main road rather than an unrelated through-road that should have used a common junction instead -- requires judging real-world road classification and topological intent (driveway/parking spur vs. genuine intersecting street), which the spec itself flags as a distinct concern ("Virtual junctions shall not replace common junctions and crossings that connect multiple roads") but does not reduce to any link-graph or attribute test. The second sentence ("The main road has priority if not specified otherwise") is default run-time semantics for a consuming simulator, not an authoring constraint, so nothing about it is checkable in the XML at all.
